captainNotes: Messi was named Barcelona's captain in 2018. While playing for the club, he won a club-record 34 trophies, including 10 La Liga titles and four UEFA Champions Leagues. With Barcelona, he set records for most goals for a single club (672) and most goals in La Liga (474). Financial difficulties at Barcelona forced Messi to depart in 2021 and sign with Ligue 1 club Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title twice. He joined the MLS club Inter Miami in 2023 and led them to their first MLS Cup victory in 2025, while also winning the league MVP award in 2024 and 2025. Following his arrival and impact on football in the United States, Messi was named Time's Athlete of the Year in 2023 and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by US president Joe Biden in 2025.

At the beginning of the 2008–09 season – his first under Barcelona's new manager, former captain Pep Guardiola – Messi was given the number 10 shirt.[77] Over time, he effectively became the tactical focal point of Guardiola's strategy, increasing his goalscoring rate as a result.[78] During that season, Messi scored 38 goals, and alongside Samuel Eto'o and Thierry Henry, contributed to a total of 100 goals in all competitions, a record at the time for the club.[79][80] Messi played in his first final as Barcelona won the Copa del Rey.[81] Barcelona also won the La Liga title and the Champions League, thus achieving the first treble in the history of Spanish football.[82]

For the start of the 2012–13 season, Barcelona had virtually secured their La Liga title by the start of 2013.[110] A double scored against Real Betis saw Messi becoming Barcelona's all-time top scorer in La Liga, and surpassed Gerd Müller's record of most goals scored in a calendar year; Messi scored a record 91 goals in all competitions for Barcelona and Argentina throughout 2012.[111][112] Messi again won the FIFA Ballon d'Or, becoming the first player in history to win the Ballon d'Or four times.[112][113] He signed a new contract committing himself to the club through 2018, and wore the captain's armband for the first time in a league match against Rayo Vallecano.[M] The team won La Liga again that year, Messi's sixth, equalling Real Madrid's 100-point record of the previous season. With 60 goals in all competitions, including 46 goals in La Liga, he finished the campaign as league top scorer in Spain and Europe for the second consecutive year, becoming the first player in history to win the European Golden Shoe three times.[117]

Messi signed a new deal with Barcelona on 25 November 2017, keeping him with the club through 2021.[149] The 2017–18 season saw Barcelona winning La Liga and the Copa del Rey once again.[150] Messi again finished the season as the top scorer in La Liga, with 34 goals, and won his fifth European Golden Shoe award.[151] With the departure of captain Andrés Iniesta in May 2018, Messi was named the team's new captain for the 2018–19 season.[152] He lifted his first trophy as Barcelona's captain, the Supercopa de España, following a 2–1 victory over Sevilla. He also helped Barcelona clinch the La Liga title.[153] With 36 goals in 34 appearances that season, Messi won his sixth La Liga Golden Shoe trophy.[154][155] He also captured his sixth European Golden Shoe award, setting a record for winning the award three seasons in a row.[156]

After Messi joined Inter Miami, the club's games began selling out.[189][190] The frenzy over his arrival was dubbed "Messimania", and Inter Miami's No. 10 Messi jersey became the best-selling jersey in the league, and nearly the best-selling in the world.[191] Messi was made the team captain of his new club, and began the 2023 season by scoring nine goals in his first six games. He led Inter Miami to their first-ever trophy as they defeated Nashville SC in the Leagues Cup final.[192][193] Miami missed the MLS playoffs, however, finishing second to last in the Eastern Conference.[194] On 30 October 2023, following his World Cup win with Argentina and Ligue 1 trophy with Paris Saint-Germain, Messi was awarded a record eighth Ballon d'Or.[195] He was also named Time Athlete of the Year, the first footballer ever to win the award.[196]

With the international retirement of Juan Román Riquelme in 2009, Messi was given Argentina's number 10 shirt.[222] Argentina built their team around Messi ahead of the 2010 FIFA World Cup and 2011 Copa América; Messi scored no goals during either tournament, as the team suffered quarter-final exits on both occasions.[223][224] At 24 years old, Messi became captain of the national team, but over the next several years was unable to lead Argentina to a trophy.[225] During the 2014 FIFA World Cup, Argentina lost to Germany in the final, though Messi was awarded the Golden Ball.[226][227] The following year, Argentina lost to Chile in the 2015 Copa América final; Messi was reportedly selected to receive the Golden Ball, but he rejected the honour.[228] During a semi-final match against the United States during the 2016 Copa América Centenario, Messi became Argentina's all-time leading goalscorer in international matches.[229] Argentina won the semi-final but lost again to Chile in the final.[230]
internationalNotes: Messi is the all-time leading goalscorer (126) and most-capped player (208) of the Argentina national team. Several years after his senior debut in 2005, he won the gold medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics. Assuming captaincy in 2011, he led Argentina to the finals of the 2014 World Cup, the 2015 Copa América, and the 2016 Copa América Centenario, all of which they lost. He subsequently announced his retirement from international football, but returned soon after. Messi led Argentina to victory at the 2021 Copa América, the 2022 World Cup, (where he became the first player to win the World Cup Golden Ball twice) and the 2024 Copa América. He led Argentina to their second consecutive World Cup final at the 2026 World Cup, where he won the Silver Ball and his second consecutive Silver Boot. Messi retired from international football on 6 October 2026.

Messi continued to progress through his club's ranks at a rapid pace, debuting for four youth teams during the 2003–04 season.[54] After being named player of the tournament in four separate international pre-season competitions with the Juvenil B, he played only one official match with the team before being promoted to the Juvenil A. In the Juvenil A he scored 18 goals in 11 league games.[55][56] During the international break, Messi was one of several youth players called up to strengthen the depleted first team. Ludovic Giuly, one of Barcelona's wingers, described Messi's performance during a training session: "He destroyed us all ... He would dribble past four players and score a goal. Even the team's starting centre-backs were nervous ... He was an alien."[57]

As a citizen of both Argentina and Spain, Messi was eligible to play for both national teams.[211] He began his international career in 2004 with Argentina's U20 team, and was subsequently included in the squad for the 2005 South American U-20 Championship, in which they finished third.[212] Messi then led the team to victory in the 2005 FIFA World Youth Championship. He finished the tournament with six goals and two assists, and won the Golden Ball.[O]

Messi made his debut with the senior national team in 2005, at age 18,[216] and scored his first international goal in a 2006 friendly against Croatia.[217][218] At the 2006 FIFA World Cup, he became the youngest player to represent and score for Argentina at the World Cup, where he scored in his debut match.[219] Messi was named the best young player of the 2007 Copa América, during which he scored two goals and provided one assist.[220] At the 2008 Summer Olympics, Messi led Argentina's U23 team to claim the Olympic gold medal over Nigeria; he was singled out by FIFA as the stand-out player from the tournament's best team.[221]

With the international retirement of Juan Román Riquelme in 2009, Messi was given Argentina's number 10 shirt.[222] Argentina built their team around Messi ahead of the 2010 FIFA World Cup and 2011 Copa América; Messi scored no goals during either tournament, as the team suffered quarter-final exits on both occasions.[223][224] At 24 years old, Messi became captain of the national team, but over the next several years was unable to lead Argentina to a trophy.[225] During the 2014 FIFA World Cup, Argentina lost to Germany in the final, though Messi was awarded the Golden Ball.[226][227] The following year, Argentina lost to Chile in the 2015 Copa América final; Messi was reportedly selected to receive the Golden Ball, but he rejected the honour.[228] During a semi-final match against the United States during the 2016 Copa América Centenario, Messi became Argentina's all-time leading goalscorer in international matches.[229] Argentina won the semi-final but lost again to Chile in the final.[230]

Losing three finals in three consecutive years caused Messi to retire from international football,[230] but a nationwide campaign in Argentina helped convince him to return to the national team to lead them to the 2018 FIFA World Cup.[231] Argentina were in jeopardy of missing the tournament on the last game of the qualifiers against Ecuador, but a hat-trick from Messi secured their entry.[232] They went on to lose to France in the round of 16 during the World Cup, with Messi scoring one goal and making two assists in the tournament.[233] The next year, Messi contributed one goal and one assist at the 2019 Copa América. Argentina finished the tournament in third place after defeating Chile, a victory which marked the start of a 36-game winning streak for the team that lasted for more than three years.[234][235]

Messi led his team to the end of a 28-year trophy drought in the 2021 Copa América, during which he surpassed Javier Mascherano for most international appearances for Argentina.[236][237] Messi's team defeated Brazil in the final, and he was named the player of the tournament, having either scored or assisted nine of Argentina's 12 goals.[236] He led Argentina to another victory over Italy at the 2022 Finalissima, where he was named player of the match, providing two assists in the 3–0 win.[238] At the 2022 FIFA World Cup, Messi led Argentina to their first World Cup victory in 36 years, scoring twice in the final to defeat France.[239] Having scored seven goals and assisted three during the tournament, Messi again won the World Cup's Golden Ball, becoming the first player to win it twice.[240]

In 2023, Messi became the third male player to reach 100 international goals. Later that year, he became the all-time top goalscorer in CONMEBOL World Cup qualifiers.[241][242] In 2024, Argentina won the Copa América for a second consecutive time,[213] with Messi setting a new record for most appearances at Copa América tournaments, with 39.[243] Later that year, he became the all-time top assist-provider in men's international football.[244][245] At the 2026 FIFA World Cup, he registered eight goals and four assists, overtaking Miroslav Klose and Marta to become the all-time leading World Cup goalscorer of any gender, before his record was surpassed by Kylian Mbappé later in the tournament.[P] He also set a new record for the most assists in World Cup history (12) since records began in 1966.[249] Messi led Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final, where they lost 1–0 to Spain in extra time.[246] He was awarded the Silver Boot as the second-highest goalscorer of the tournament, and won the Silver Ball as the second-best player.[250]

On 31 August 2026, Messi announced his retirement from international football.[251] However, he was called up to the national team again to play one final match against Benin at Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on 6 October.[252] Messi contributed to every goal in the 3–0 victory, assisting the first two before scoring his final international goal on a penalty.[253]

Messi received dismissals by critics throughout his career because he had not won an international tournament at the senior level with Argentina.[AA] However, his subsequent victories in the 2021 Copa América and the 2022 FIFA World Cup resulted in him finally winning every top tier trophy at both the club and country levels, an achievement that many pundits felt cemented Messi's legacy.[289]

Throughout his career, Messi has been compared with Diego Maradona, who was also considered the best player of his generation and one of the greatest in the history of the sport.[338][339] The comparisons stem broadly from both players' short statures, their similar playing styles as left-footed playmakers, and their shared nationality as Argentines.[340] Initially, Messi was merely one of many young Argentine players to receive the "New Maradona" moniker, but as his career progressed, he proved his similarity beyond all previous contenders, establishing himself as the best player Argentina had produced since Maradona.[44][341] When Messi was 18 years old, Maradona called him the best player in the world and hailed him as his successor.[342] From 2008 through the 2010 FIFA World Cup, Messi played for Argentina's national team with Maradona as his manager, and it was during this period that Messi was given the number 10 shirt that Maradona famously wore. Maradona gave Messi his blessing, telling him: "the No 10 is yours. There's nobody better than you to wear it."[222]

During the early and middle parts of Messi's career, he was generally held in lesser esteem than Maradona in Argentine society. Part of this had to do with Messi's lack of international tournament success and perceived uneven output with the national team; Maradona had famously led Argentina to victory in the 1986 FIFA World Cup, which set an expectation for Messi to do the same.[AC] Argentines also identified more with the fiery, extroverted and controversial Maradona who came from the slums, as opposed to the reserved, introverted and unassuming Messi who had a comparably unremarkable upbringing in Rosario.[AD] Maradona, along with several pundits and footballing figures, questioned whether Messi's temperament made him a capable leader for the national team.[AE] Furthermore, Messi's lack of outward passion for the Argentina shirt, his early tendency not to sing the national anthem, and his relative lack of emotional displays have led to a perception that he feels more Catalan than Argentine.[224][346] However, despite having lived in Barcelona since age 13, Messi rejected the option of representing Spain internationally, saying: "Argentina is my country, my family, my way of expressing myself. I would change all my records to make the people in my country happy."[347]

Messi was among the Time 100, an annual list of the world's most influential people, in 2011, 2012 and 2023.[AF] According to a 2014 survey in 15 international markets, Messi was familiar to 87% of respondents around the world, of whom 78% perceived him favourably, making him the second-most recognised player globally, behind Cristiano Ronaldo, and the most likeable of all contemporary players.[355][356] World Press Photo selected "The Final Game", a photo of Messi facing the World Cup trophy after Argentina's final defeat to Germany, as the best sports image of 2014.[357]

Messi, a documentary directed by Álex de la Iglesia, premiered at the 71st Venice International Film Festival in August 2014.[410] Messi's World Cup: The Rise of a Legend, a biographical docuseries focusing on Messi's career, his highs and lows with the Argentina national football team, and their eventual success at the 2022 FIFA World Cup, aired on Apple TV+ on 21 February 2024.[411]

Since leaving for Spain at age 13, Messi has maintained close ties to Rosario, and has preserved his Rosarino accent. He has retained ownership of his family's old house, although it has long stood empty, and he maintains a penthouse apartment in an exclusive residential building for his mother, as well as a family compound just outside the city. Messi keeps in frequent contact with a small group of confidants in Rosario, most of whom were fellow members of "The Machine of '87" at Newell's Old Boys. He was on bad terms with the club after his transfer to Barcelona, but by 2012 their public feud had ended, with Newell's embracing their ties with Messi and issuing a club membership card to his newborn son.[AK] Messi has long planned to end his playing career at Newell's.[449] Messi has citizenship in Argentina, Italy, and Spain.[450]
ratingNotes: Messi is the most decorated player in the history of professional football, having won 47 team trophies[E] across more than 1,200 career appearances.[25] He has scored over 930 senior career goals and provided over 420 assists for club and country, making him the second-highest goalscorer and the highest assist provider in the history of football. He was ranked as the world's highest-paid athlete by Forbes in 2019 and 2022. In 2020, he became the second footballer to surpass $1 billion in career earnings.

In 2004, Messi made his competitive debut for the La Liga club Barcelona at age 17. He was awarded the FIFPRO Young Player of the Year in 2006, 2007 and 2008. During the 2008–09 season, he helped Barcelona achieve the first treble in Spanish football, earning him the first of four consecutive Ballons d'Or. By the 2011–12 season he had set the European record for most goals in a season and was Barcelona's all-time top scorer. During the 2014–15 season, Messi was part of the attacking trio MSN with Luis Suárez and Neymar, and helped Barcelona achieve a historic second treble.

Messi was named Barcelona's captain in 2018. While playing for the club, he won a club-record 34 trophies, including 10 La Liga titles and four UEFA Champions Leagues. With Barcelona, he set records for most goals for a single club (672) and most goals in La Liga (474). Financial difficulties at Barcelona forced Messi to depart in 2021 and sign with Ligue 1 club Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title twice. He joined the MLS club Inter Miami in 2023 and led them to their first MLS Cup victory in 2025, while also winning the league MVP award in 2024 and 2025. Following his arrival and impact on football in the United States, Messi was named Time's Athlete of the Year in 2023 and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by US president Joe Biden in 2025.

At the age of four, Messi joined the local football club Abanderado Grandoli where he was coached by his father. His maternal grandmother, Celia, accompanied him to training and matches.[31] He was greatly affected by her death, shortly before his eleventh birthday. Since then, as a devout Catholic, he has celebrated his goals by looking up and pointing to the sky in tribute to his grandmother.[32][33] Messi has a general understanding of English but cannot speak it fluently,[34] and has expressed regret for refusing to learn the language during his childhood.[35]

Messi started playing for the Rosario-based football club Newell's Old Boys when he was seven years old; he would become a lifelong supporter of the club. During the six years he played for Newell's, he scored almost 500 goals, and was a member of "The Machine of '87", a nearly unbeatable youth team named for the year of their birth. Messi regularly entertained crowds by performing ball tricks during half-time, when the Newell's first team played home games.[F] His goalscoring idol growing up was Brazilian striker Ronaldo, who Messi called "the best forward I've ever seen".[40]

Messi's future as a professional player was threatened when, at the age of 10, he was diagnosed with a growth hormone deficiency. He began growth hormone therapy at age 11;[41] however, his father's health insurance covered only two years of the therapy, which cost at least 1,000 pesos per month. Newell's agreed to contribute, but later reneged on their promise.[42] Messi was scouted by the Buenos Aires club River Plate, whose playmaker Pablo Aimar he idolised.[43][44] It was speculated for a time that Messi failed to sign with River Plate due to his ill health; however, in a 2019 interview, he revealed that River Plate had wanted to sign him after he scored four goals at a trial, and even offered to pay for his medical treatment, but Newell's refused to release his player card, preventing the transfer.[45]

After a year at Barcelona's youth academy, La Masia, Messi was enrolled in the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) in February 2002. He could now play in all competitions, and he quickly befriended his teammates, including Cesc Fàbregas and Gerard Piqué.[48] After completing his growth hormone therapy at age 14,[49] Messi became an integral part of the "Baby Dream Team", which has been lauded as Barcelona's greatest-ever youth team. During his first full season (2002–03), he was the top scorer with 36 goals in 30 games for the Cadetes A, who won an unprecedented treble of the league, the Spanish cup, and the Copa Catalunya.[48][50] In the Copa Catalunya final, their 4–1 victory over Espanyol came to be referred to in club lore as the partido de la máscara, the "final of the mask". A week after suffering a broken cheekbone during a league match, Messi was allowed to play on the condition that he wear a protective plastic mask. When the mask became a hindrance, Messi took it off and scored two goals within 10 minutes.[51] At the end of the season, he received an offer to join the English football club Arsenal, but he chose to remain in Barcelona.[H]

Messi continued to progress through his club's ranks at a rapid pace, debuting for four youth teams during the 2003–04 season.[54] After being named player of the tournament in four separate international pre-season competitions with the Juvenil B, he played only one official match with the team before being promoted to the Juvenil A. In the Juvenil A he scored 18 goals in 11 league games.[55][56] During the international break, Messi was one of several youth players called up to strengthen the depleted first team. Ludovic Giuly, one of Barcelona's wingers, described Messi's performance during a training session: "He destroyed us all ... He would dribble past four players and score a goal. Even the team's starting centre-backs were nervous ... He was an alien."[57]

To gain further match experience, Messi joined his club's third team, Barcelona C, in addition to the Juvenil A. He helped save the third team from the relegation zone of the Tercera División, scoring five goals in ten games, including a hat-trick in eight minutes during a Copa del Rey Juvenil match.[55][63] His progress was reflected in his first professional contract, signed on 4 February 2004, which lasted until 2012 and contained an initial buyout clause of €30 million. A month later, he made his debut for Barcelona B in the Segunda División B, and his buyout clause automatically increased to €80 million.[55][64] He played five games with the B team that season but did not score.[65] He was physically weaker than his opponents, who were often much older and taller, and he worked on increasing his muscle mass and overall strength. Towards the end of the season, he returned to both youth teams, helping the Juvenil B win the league. He finished the campaign having scored goals for four of his five teams, with a total of 36 goals in all official competitions.[55][63]

Messi began the 2004–05 season as a guaranteed starter for the Barcelona B team, but after some lobbying by the senior players, he was promoted to the first team by manager Frank Rijkaard.[60] He made his La Liga debut for Barcelona on 16 October 2004, at 17 years old.[46] He scored his first senior goal on 1 May 2005, becoming the youngest-ever scorer for the club at the time.[66][67] He was at that time the youngest player to represent Barcelona in an official competition, and the club won the league title during that season.[62][68]

During the 2006–07 season, Messi scored his first hat-trick during a game against Real Madrid, becoming the first player to score a hat-trick in a Clásico in 12 years.[73] Two goals scored by Messi against Getafe and Espanyol during the season drew notice for their similarities to two famous goals scored by fellow Argentine Diego Maradona in the 1986 World Cup match against England, leading to comparisons between Messi and Maradona that would endure throughout Messi's career.[I] Barcelona finished the 2006–07 season with only one trophy – the 2006 Supercopa de España – and the 2007–08 season without a single trophy, leading to Rijkaard's departure.[76]

At the beginning of the 2008–09 season – his first under Barcelona's new manager, former captain Pep Guardiola – Messi was given the number 10 shirt.[77] Over time, he effectively became the tactical focal point of Guardiola's strategy, increasing his goalscoring rate as a result.[78] During that season, Messi scored 38 goals, and alongside Samuel Eto'o and Thierry Henry, contributed to a total of 100 goals in all competitions, a record at the time for the club.[79][80] Messi played in his first final as Barcelona won the Copa del Rey.[81] Barcelona also won the La Liga title and the Champions League, thus achieving the first treble in the history of Spanish football.[82]

During the first half of the 2009–10 season, Barcelona won the Supercopa de España, the UEFA Super Cup and the FIFA Club World Cup, becoming the first club to achieve the sextuple.[83][84] Messi finished as the Champions League top scorer, the youngest in the tournament's history.[85][86] For his efforts in 2009, Messi won the Ballon d'Or, the FIFA World Player of the Year award and his first European Golden Shoe.[J] He scored a total of 47 goals in all competitions, equalling Ronaldo's club record from the 1996–97 campaign.[90][87] He signed a new 7-year contract with Barcelona through 2016.[69]

During the 2010–11 season, Barcelona won the Supercopa de España,[91] the Champions League,[92] and a third consecutive La Liga title. Messi's club performances in 2010 earned him his second consecutive Ballon d'Or.[93] He was the top scorer in the Champions League for the third consecutive year,[94] and the league's top scorer and assist provider.[95][96] He became Barcelona's all-time single-season top scorer with 53 goals.[K] During the 2011–12 season, Barcelona won both the Spanish and European Super Cup trophies, as well as the FIFA Club World Cup.[L] Messi won the Golden Ball for the second time[101] and the Ballon d'Or for the third time,[102] as well as the inaugural UEFA Best Player in Europe Award.[103] During 2012, Messi became the second player to be top scorer in four Champions League campaigns.[104][105] He became the top goalscorer in Barcelona's history at age 24, overtaking César Rodríguez's 57-year record of 232 goals.[106] He finished the season as the league top scorer in Spain for the second time with 50 goals, a La Liga record. His 73 goals in all competitions made him the single-season top scorer in the history of European club football excluding regional and local competitions.[107][108] Barcelona won the Copa del Rey that season, their 14th trophy under Guardiola, who resigned after a four-year cycle of success.[109]

For the start of the 2012–13 season, Barcelona had virtually secured their La Liga title by the start of 2013.[110] A double scored against Real Betis saw Messi becoming Barcelona's all-time top scorer in La Liga, and surpassed Gerd Müller's record of most goals scored in a calendar year; Messi scored a record 91 goals in all competitions for Barcelona and Argentina throughout 2012.[111][112] Messi again won the FIFA Ballon d'Or, becoming the first player in history to win the Ballon d'Or four times.[112][113] He signed a new contract committing himself to the club through 2018, and wore the captain's armband for the first time in a league match against Rayo Vallecano.[M] The team won La Liga again that year, Messi's sixth, equalling Real Madrid's 100-point record of the previous season. With 60 goals in all competitions, including 46 goals in La Liga, he finished the campaign as league top scorer in Spain and Europe for the second consecutive year, becoming the first player in history to win the European Golden Shoe three times.[117]

Messi's overall input into the team's attack had increased significantly. Whereas he contributed to 24% of the team's goals in their treble-winning campaign in 2008–09, this number rose to more than 40% by the end of the 2012–13 season.[118] These statistics, as well as lopsided losses in the Champions League where Messi was unfit, gave credence to the notion of Messidependencia, Barcelona's perceived tactical and psychological dependence on their star player.[119]

To offset the load on Messi, Barcelona signed Brazilian forward Neymar from Santos before the 2013–14 season.[120] The team won the Supercopa de España at the beginning of the season.[121] Messi finished the campaign with his worst output in five seasons, though he still managed to score 41 goals in all competitions.[122] For the first time in five years, Barcelona ended the season without a major trophy.[123]

A hat-trick by Messi against Sevilla in November 2014 made him the all-time top scorer in La Liga, as he surpassed the 59-year record of 251 league goals held by Telmo Zarra.[130] After securing the La Liga title, the Copa del Rey, and the Champions League that year, Messi helped Barcelona become the first club to win the continental treble twice.[131][132] Messi recorded 58 goals during the season, while the MSN trio scored a total of 122 goals in all competitions, a record in Spanish football.[133]

Messi opened the 2015–16 season by helping Barcelona defeat Sevilla in the UEFA Super Cup.[134] He finished 2015 by winning the FIFA Club World Cup, defeating River Plate in the final and collecting his fifth club trophy of the calendar year.[135] In January 2016, he won the FIFA Ballon d'Or for a record fifth time in his career,[136] and he finished the season by winning both La Liga and the Copa del Rey again.[137] Messi scored 41 goals during the season, while the MSN trio scored a total of 131 goals, breaking the record they had set the previous season.[138]

The 2016–17 season ended with Barcelona winning the Supercopa de España and the Copa del Rey.[139][140] Messi finished the season with 54 goals, while his 37 goals in La Liga saw him claim both the Pichichi and European Golden Shoe Awards for the fourth time in his career.[141] MSN came to be regarded as one of the greatest attacking trios in the game,[147] and ended with Neymar's August 2017 transfer to Paris Saint-Germain.[148]

Messi signed a new deal with Barcelona on 25 November 2017, keeping him with the club through 2021.[149] The 2017–18 season saw Barcelona winning La Liga and the Copa del Rey once again.[150] Messi again finished the season as the top scorer in La Liga, with 34 goals, and won his fifth European Golden Shoe award.[151] With the departure of captain Andrés Iniesta in May 2018, Messi was named the team's new captain for the 2018–19 season.[152] He lifted his first trophy as Barcelona's captain, the Supercopa de España, following a 2–1 victory over Sevilla. He also helped Barcelona clinch the La Liga title.[153] With 36 goals in 34 appearances that season, Messi won his sixth La Liga Golden Shoe trophy.[154][155] He also captured his sixth European Golden Shoe award, setting a record for winning the award three seasons in a row.[156]

Messi won his sixth Ballon d'Or, but the subsequent 2019–20 season saw Barcelona go trophyless for the first time since 2007–08.[157] Following a disappointing season, Messi expressed to the club his desire to leave, but ultimately decided to fulfill the final year of his contract.[158][159] In 2021, he led Barcelona to victory in the Copa del Rey.[160][161] His last two seasons with Barcelona saw him lead La Liga in goal scoring, giving him a record-breaking total of eight Pichichi trophies.[162][163] With 30 goals in the 2020–21 La Liga campaign and a triumph with Argentina at the 2021 Copa América, where he was jointly named Best Player and won the Golden Boot, Messi was awarded the 2021 Ballon d'Or.[164]

On 10 August 2021, two days after his farewell remarks to Barcelona, Messi joined the Ligue 1 club Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) on a two-year contract with an option for an extra year.[170][171] He chose 30 as his squad number, which is the number he wore when he made his senior debut for Barcelona.[172] He scored his first goal for the club in a Champions League group stage win over former manager Pep Guardiola's Manchester City.[173] Messi won his first Ligue 1 title, which was a recording-tying 10th league title for PSG.[174] Overall, he had an underwhelming season, scoring 6 goals in the league.[175][176]

Near the start of the 2022–23 season, Messi won his second trophy with PSG in the Trophée des Champions.[177] A goal against Nice saw him surpass Cristiano Ronaldo as the all-time highest goalscorer in European club football with 702 goals; during the match, he also achieved 1,000 career goal contributions (goals scored and assists served) at the club level.[178][179] By the end of the Ligue 1 season, he had scored 16 goals and had the highest number of assists with 16, which helped PSG clinch their 11th Ligue 1 title and Messi's second in a row.[N] Messi was awarded the Ligue 1 Best Foreign Player of the Season and was recognised as the season's best player in Europe, according to Opta data.[183][184] At the end of the season, he departed PSG.[185]

On 15 July 2023, the Major League Soccer (MLS) club Inter Miami CF announced the signing of Messi on a two-and-a-half-year contract.[186][187] Messi's pay set an MLS record, with his earnings from salary, signing bonus, and an equity stake in the club reportedly surpassing $50 million.[188] According to Goal, Messi's arrival in the United States helped to raise the profile of MLS within the US and abroad. Inter Miami co-president Xavier Asensi said that for MLS "there is a before and after Messi. He has changed everything."

After Messi joined Inter Miami, the club's games began selling out.[189][190] The frenzy over his arrival was dubbed "Messimania", and Inter Miami's No. 10 Messi jersey became the best-selling jersey in the league, and nearly the best-selling in the world.[191] Messi was made the team captain of his new club, and began the 2023 season by scoring nine goals in his first six games. He led Inter Miami to their first-ever trophy as they defeated Nashville SC in the Leagues Cup final.[192][193] Miami missed the MLS playoffs, however, finishing second to last in the Eastern Conference.[194] On 30 October 2023, following his World Cup win with Argentina and Ligue 1 trophy with Paris Saint-Germain, Messi was awarded a record eighth Ballon d'Or.[195] He was also named Time Athlete of the Year, the first footballer ever to win the award.[196]

During the 2024 season, Messi broke the record for the most assists in a single MLS game with five assists.[197] On 2 October, he scored two goals in a 3–2 win over the Columbus Crew, clinching the Supporters' Shield award for Miami.[198] In the final game of the season, Messi scored his first hat-trick for the club in a 6–2 victory. Miami finished the regular season with 74 points, an MLS league record, while Messi finished with 20 goals and 16 assists in 19 matches, becoming the all-time top goalscorer for the young team.[199][200] Miami made their first postseason appearance in the 2024 MLS Cup playoffs but was eliminated in the first round.[201] Messi was named the MLS Most Valuable Player for the season.[202]

During the 2025 season, Messi became the fastest player in MLS history to reach 40 league goals.[203] He ended the season by winning the MLS Golden Boot as the league's top scorer, with 29 goals and 19 assists in 28 games.[202] On 23 October, he signed a contract extension with the club through 2028, by which time he would be 41 years old.[204] During the Eastern Conference final against New York City FC in the 2025 MLS Cup playoffs, an assist from Messi put his career assists across all competitions at 405, surpassing Ferenc Puskás for the most career assists of all time.[205][206] Messi led Miami to MLS Cup 2025, where they won 3–1 over the Vancouver Whitecaps to win the team's first league championship. Providing two assists during the match, Messi was named MLS Cup MVP.[207] At the end of the season, Messi was again named MLS MVP, becoming the first player in league history to win the award in back-to-back years.[202]

In March 2026 it was reported that Messi was earning between $70 and $80 million per year from Inter Miami from his compensation and equity rights.[208] On 18 March 2026, Messi scored his 900th career goal during Inter Miami's 1–1 draw with Nashville in the CONCACAF Champions Cup. He became the second player to reach the mark in top-level men's football after Cristiano Ronaldo.[209][210]

As a citizen of both Argentina and Spain, Messi was eligible to play for both national teams.[211] He began his international career in 2004 with Argentina's U20 team, and was subsequently included in the squad for the 2005 South American U-20 Championship, in which they finished third.[212] Messi then led the team to victory in the 2005 FIFA World Youth Championship. He finished the tournament with six goals and two assists, and won the Golden Ball.[O]

Messi made his debut with the senior national team in 2005, at age 18,[216] and scored his first international goal in a 2006 friendly against Croatia.[217][218] At the 2006 FIFA World Cup, he became the youngest player to represent and score for Argentina at the World Cup, where he scored in his debut match.[219] Messi was named the best young player of the 2007 Copa América, during which he scored two goals and provided one assist.[220] At the 2008 Summer Olympics, Messi led Argentina's U23 team to claim the Olympic gold medal over Nigeria; he was singled out by FIFA as the stand-out player from the tournament's best team.[221]

With the international retirement of Juan Román Riquelme in 2009, Messi was given Argentina's number 10 shirt.[222] Argentina built their team around Messi ahead of the 2010 FIFA World Cup and 2011 Copa América; Messi scored no goals during either tournament, as the team suffered quarter-final exits on both occasions.[223][224] At 24 years old, Messi became captain of the national team, but over the next several years was unable to lead Argentina to a trophy.[225] During the 2014 FIFA World Cup, Argentina lost to Germany in the final, though Messi was awarded the Golden Ball.[226][227] The following year, Argentina lost to Chile in the 2015 Copa América final; Messi was reportedly selected to receive the Golden Ball, but he rejected the honour.[228] During a semi-final match against the United States during the 2016 Copa América Centenario, Messi became Argentina's all-time leading goalscorer in international matches.[229] Argentina won the semi-final but lost again to Chile in the final.[230]

Losing three finals in three consecutive years caused Messi to retire from international football,[230] but a nationwide campaign in Argentina helped convince him to return to the national team to lead them to the 2018 FIFA World Cup.[231] Argentina were in jeopardy of missing the tournament on the last game of the qualifiers against Ecuador, but a hat-trick from Messi secured their entry.[232] They went on to lose to France in the round of 16 during the World Cup, with Messi scoring one goal and making two assists in the tournament.[233] The next year, Messi contributed one goal and one assist at the 2019 Copa América. Argentina finished the tournament in third place after defeating Chile, a victory which marked the start of a 36-game winning streak for the team that lasted for more than three years.[234][235]

Messi led his team to the end of a 28-year trophy drought in the 2021 Copa América, during which he surpassed Javier Mascherano for most international appearances for Argentina.[236][237] Messi's team defeated Brazil in the final, and he was named the player of the tournament, having either scored or assisted nine of Argentina's 12 goals.[236] He led Argentina to another victory over Italy at the 2022 Finalissima, where he was named player of the match, providing two assists in the 3–0 win.[238] At the 2022 FIFA World Cup, Messi led Argentina to their first World Cup victory in 36 years, scoring twice in the final to defeat France.[239] Having scored seven goals and assisted three during the tournament, Messi again won the World Cup's Golden Ball, becoming the first player to win it twice.[240]

In 2023, Messi became the third male player to reach 100 international goals. Later that year, he became the all-time top goalscorer in CONMEBOL World Cup qualifiers.[241][242] In 2024, Argentina won the Copa América for a second consecutive time,[213] with Messi setting a new record for most appearances at Copa América tournaments, with 39.[243] Later that year, he became the all-time top assist-provider in men's international football.[244][245] At the 2026 FIFA World Cup, he registered eight goals and four assists, overtaking Miroslav Klose and Marta to become the all-time leading World Cup goalscorer of any gender, before his record was surpassed by Kylian Mbappé later in the tournament.[P] He also set a new record for the most assists in World Cup history (12) since records began in 1966.[249] Messi led Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final, where they lost 1–0 to Spain in extra time.[246] He was awarded the Silver Boot as the second-highest goalscorer of the tournament, and won the Silver Ball as the second-best player.[250]

On 31 August 2026, Messi announced his retirement from international football.[251] However, he was called up to the national team again to play one final match against Benin at Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on 6 October.[252] Messi contributed to every goal in the 3–0 victory, assisting the first two before scoring his final international goal on a penalty.[253]

Due to his short stature, Messi has a lower centre of gravity than taller players, which gives him greater agility and allows him to change direction more quickly and evade opposing tackles;[254][255] the Spanish media has dubbed him La Pulga Atómica ("The Atomic Flea").[Q] Despite being physically unimposing, Messi possesses significant upper-body strength, which, when combined with his low centre of gravity and resulting balance, aids him in withstanding physical challenges from opponents; he has consequently been noted for his lack of diving in a sport rife with playacting.[R] Messi's short, strong legs allow him short bursts of acceleration, while his quick feet enable him to retain control of the ball when dribbling at speed.[260] His former Barcelona manager Pep Guardiola once stated, "Messi is the only player that runs faster with the ball than he does without it."[261] Messi is predominantly a left-footed player, although he has improved his ability with his weaker right foot since his mid-20s. He usually begins dribbling runs with the outside of his left foot, while using the inside of that foot to score and provide passes and assists.[262][263]

A prolific goalscorer, Messi is known for his positioning, quick reactions, and ability to make attacking runs to beat the defensive line. He also functions in a playmaking role, courtesy of his vision and range of passing.[264] He has often been described as a magician, conjuring goals and opportunities where none seemingly exist.[S] He is known for the accuracy of his free kicks, and as of September 2026 he ranks second in career goals scored from direct free kicks with 76.[T] He also has a penchant for scoring from chips.[271]

Messi's pace and technical ability enable him to undertake individual dribbling runs towards the goal, in particular during counterattacks, usually starting from the halfway line or the right side of the pitch.[U] He is widely considered to be one of the greatest dribblers of all time.[273][274] Former Argentina manager Diego Maradona said of him, "The ball stays glued to his foot ... I've never seen anyone with Messi's ball control."[263] Beyond Messi's individual qualities, he is also a well-rounded, hard-working team player, known for his creative combinations, in particular with former Barcelona midfielders Xavi and Andrés Iniesta.[254][255]

Tactically, Messi plays in a free attacking role; a versatile player, he is capable of attacking on either wing or through the centre of the pitch. His favoured position in childhood was the playmaker behind two strikers, known as the enganche in Argentine football, but he began his career in Spain as a left-winger or left-sided forward.[279] Upon his first-team debut, he was moved onto the right wing by manager Frank Rijkaard; from this position, he could more easily cut through the defence into the middle of the pitch and curl shots on goal with his left foot, rather than predominantly cross balls for teammates.[261] Under Guardiola and subsequent managers, he most often played in a false nine role; positioned as a centre-forward or lone striker, he roamed the centre, often moving deep into midfield and drawing defenders with him, in order to create and exploit spaces for passes, other teammates' attacking runs off the ball, his own dribbling runs, or combinations with Xavi and Iniesta.[47]

A prodigious talent as a teenager, Messi established himself among the world's best players before age 20.[291] After winning the 2005 Ballon d'Or, Messi's teammate Ronaldinho remarked, "I'm not even the best at Barça" in reference to the 18-year-old Messi.[292] Four years later, after Messi won his first Ballon d'Or by a record margin,[89] the public debate regarding his qualities as a player moved beyond his status in contemporary football to the possibility that he was one of the greatest players in history.[W] An early proponent was his then-Barcelona manager Pep Guardiola, who, as early as August 2009, described Messi as the best player he had ever seen and would ever see.[294] In the following years, this opinion gained greater acceptance among pundits, managers, former and current players.[97][295] By the end of Barcelona's second treble-winning season, the perception of Messi as one of the greatest footballers of all time had become the apparent view among many fans and pundits in continental Europe.[296][297]

Among his contemporary peers, Messi is most often compared and contrasted with Cristiano Ronaldo, who many consider his career rival.[288] Both achieved numerous individual accolades, won dozens of trophies for both club and country, and are the two leading goal scorers in history. Although Messi has at times denied any rivalry,[321][322] they are widely believed to push one another in their aim to be the best player in the world.[323] Pundits have compared the ongoing rivalry to past sports rivalries like the Muhammad Ali–Joe Frazier rivalry in boxing, the Prost–Senna rivalry in motorsport, and the tennis rivalries between Federer–Nadal and Borg–McEnroe.[324]

Messi's head-to-head record against teams that feature Ronaldo consists of 15 wins, 9 draws, and 10 losses in competitive club matches. The first competitive matchup between the two occurred in 2008, when Ronaldo's Manchester United played Messi's Barcelona in the 2007–08 UEFA Champions League semi-finals; Manchester United advanced and eventually won the final.[332] The two players and their club teams met again in the next year's Champions League final, with Messi and Barcelona achieving a 2–0 victory.[333] After this, Ronaldo transferred to Real Madrid, the main rivals of Barcelona, which resulted in Messi facing Ronaldo many times in El Clásico, which ranks among the world's most viewed annual sports events.[334][331] A number of football critics, commentators, and players have said that Messi's triumph with Argentina in the 2022 World Cup has settled the contest between the two players.[AB]

In 2013, a Turkish Airlines advertisement starring Messi and Kobe Bryant became the most-watched advertisement on YouTube, with 137 million views. It was voted by users as the best advertisement of the decade 2005–2015.[396][397] In June 2021, Messi signed a five-year deal to become a brand ambassador for Hard Rock Cafe,[398] and the following year he became a tourism ambassador for Saudi Arabia. He was criticised for partnering with Saudi Arabia because of the country's poor record on human rights.[399][400]

In November 2016, while the Argentine Football Association was being run by a FIFA committee due to an economic crisis, three of the national team's security staff told Messi that they had not received their salaries for six months. He paid the salaries of the three employees.[432][433] In February 2021, Messi made a donation to the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya: the Adidas shoes he wore when he scored his 644th goal for Barcelona and broke Pelé's record for most goals scored for a single club. The museum later auctioned off the shoes for £125,000 to support a charity focused on children with cancer.[434]

captainNotes: Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 at the age of 18. He helped them reach the final of Euro 2004, and was named captain ahead of Euro 2008. He led Portugal to victory at Euro 2016 and at the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025. Ronaldo holds the records for most international appearances (234),[7] most men's international goals (146), and most international victories (141). He was named in the UEFA Ultimate Team of the Year in 2015, the All-time UEFA Euro XI in 2016, and the Ballon d'Or Dream Team in 2020. In recognition of his record-breaking goalscoring success, he received special FIFA awards for Outstanding Career Achievement in 2021.

On 30 December 2022, Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr reached an agreement for Ronaldo to join the club, signing a contract until 2025.[183] Ronaldo received the highest football salary ever, at €200 million per year,[184][185] including a guaranteed football salary of €90 million, with commercial and sponsorship deals bringing his total annual salary to €200 million. He made his debut for Al-Nassr on 22 January 2023, as club captain, playing the full 90 minutes of a 1–0 win over Al-Ettifaq,[186] and scored his first goal in a 2–2 draw against Al-Fateh by converting a last-minute penalty.[187] On 9 February, Ronaldo scored all four goals in a 4–0 win over Al-Wehda, his first goal of the match being his 500th career league goal.[188] According to the BBC, Ronaldo's transfer to Al-Nassr led a "revolution" in Asian football, with many players from other leagues, particularly those in Europe, transferring to Saudi Pro League clubs for the 2023–24 season.[189][190][191]

At the age of 18, Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal as a substitute against Kazakhstan on 20 August 2003.[209] At UEFA Euro 2004, he scored his first international goal in a 2–1 group stage loss to Greece in his eighth international appearance.[210][211] Despite Portugal losing to Greece again in the final, Ronaldo made the team of the tournament, with two assists and two goals.[212] In the 2006 FIFA World Cup, at the age of 21 years and 132 days, Ronaldo became the youngest ever goalscorer for Portugal at a World Cup finals.[213] Portugal reached the semi-finals, where Portugal lost to France, with Ronaldo being booed during their defeat, due to an incident that occurred in the quarter-finals against England.[214] FIFA's Technical Study Group overlooked him for the tournament's Best Young Player award and handed it to Germany's Lukas Podolski, citing his behaviour as a factor in the decision.[215][216]

On 23 March 2023, Ronaldo scored two goals against Liechtenstein as he earned his 197th overall cap to become the most capped male footballer of all time.[242] On 20 June, Ronaldo made his 200th appearance for his national team, scoring the only goal of an away win over Iceland, in the Euro qualifiers, as he became the first player in the history of men's international football to make 200 appearances for his country.[243] On 16 October, Portugal secured first place in their qualifying group, following a 5–0 away victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina, with Ronaldo scoring twice.[244]

With his start in Portugal's UEFA Euro 2024 opener against the Czech Republic, Ronaldo became the first player to feature in six European Championships, having previously been the first player to appear in five.[245] Later that year, on 5 September, he scored his 900th career goal in a 2–1 victory over Croatia in the UEFA Nations League.[246] On 15 November, Ronaldo broke the record of most international victories with 132, overtaking Sergio Ramos's record, following a 5–1 victory against Poland in the UEFA Nations League, where he scored twice.[247] On 8 June 2025, Ronaldo won his second Nations League title, helping Portugal defeat Spain in the final, scoring eight goals in nine games in the tournament.[248]

Jesus subsequently described the dispute as a misunderstanding, but Ronaldo accused him of breaking two promises in a statement on 6 October, while apologising and expressing his willingness to return.[263] On 10 October, the FPF provisionally suspended Ronaldo pending disciplinary proceedings, which led on 19 October, Ronaldo being fined and suspended for 30 days.[264][265]

Ronaldo first performed the "Siu" celebration on 7 August 2013, during the 2013 International Champions Cup Final between Real Madrid and Chelsea.[325] During an interview after the match, Ronaldo explained he scored the goal and "it just felt natural" and "didn't know where it came from".[326] The phrase "Siu" is derived from Portuguese sim, meaning "yes". This was confirmed by Ronaldo in an interview in 2023, almost a decade since he first performed it. Ronaldo explained that the phrase "Siuuu" simply means yes, but "meaning it very strongly".[327]

The unveiling of the rebranded Cristiano Ronaldo International Airport took place on 29 March 2017, which included a bust of his head being presented.[403] The bust and the name change were controversial, with the lack of the bust's likeness to Ronaldo being ridiculed by comedians, including Saturday Night Live,[411][403] A year later, sports website Bleacher Report commissioned sculptor Emanuel Santos to create another bust;[412] however, this bust was never used and a new one was made by a Spanish sculptor, shown to the public on 15 June 2018.[413]

Ronaldo is one of the most decorated players in the history of professional football. His 35 trophies include five UEFA Champions Leagues, two UEFA Nations Leagues and the UEFA European Championship. He is the only player to have scored 100 goals with four different clubs and to finish as the top scorer in four different domestic leagues. He has made over 1,300 professional career appearances, the most by an outfield player, and has scored over 980 official senior career goals for club and country, making him the top goalscorer in the history of the sport.

He led Portugal to victory at Euro 2016 and at the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025. Ronaldo holds the records for most international appearances (234),[7] most men's international goals (146), and most international victories (141). He was named in the UEFA Ultimate Team of the Year in 2015, the All-time UEFA Euro XI in 2016, and the Ballon d'Or Dream Team in 2020. On 14 August 2002, at age 17, Ronaldo played his first official match for the first team, in a UEFA Champions League qualifying round against Inter Milan.[41] His Primeira Liga debut occurred a month later against Braga, and on 7 October he scored two goals against Moreirense in Sporting's 3–0 win.[42] After Sporting defeated Manchester United 3–1 in a friendly on 6 August 2003, United manager Alex Ferguson was determined to acquire Ronaldo, describing him as "one of the most exciting young players" he had ever seen.[43][44]

On 12 August 2003, less than a week after the match that impressed Ferguson, Manchester United signed Ronaldo for £12 million,[45] an England record for a teenager.[46] He was the first Portuguese player to sign for the club.[45] Although he requested the number 28, his number at Sporting, he received the squad number 7 shirt, which had previously been worn by such United players as George Best, Eric Cantona and David Beckham.[47] Wearing the number 7 became an extra source of motivation for Ronaldo.[48] He would later describe Ferguson as his "father in sport" and "one of the most important and influential factors" in his career.[49]

Ronaldo made his debut for United as a substitute in a 4–0 win over Bolton Wanderers in the Premier League on 16 August 2003.[50] His performance earned praise from Best, who hailed it as "undoubtedly the most exciting debut" he had ever seen.[51] Ronaldo scored his first goal for the club from a free kick in a 3–0 win over Portsmouth on 1 November.[52] On 15 May 2004, he scored the opening goal in a victory against Aston Villa, and received the first red card of his career.[53][54] He finished his first season in England with a trophy, scoring the opening goal in United's 3–0 win over Millwall in the 2004 FA Cup Final.[55]

At the start of the 2004–05 season, Ronaldo provided a goal and an assist against Aston Villa and scored twice against Arsenal.[56][57] He won his second trophy in English football, the Football League Cup, after scoring the third goal in United's 4–0 final win over Wigan Athletic.[58] During his third season in England, Ronaldo was involved in several incidents. He clashed with his teammate Ruud van Nistelrooy, who took offence at Ronaldo's showboating style of play.[59] During the 2006 FIFA World Cup, Ronaldo was involved in an incident which resulted in his club teammate Wayne Rooney being sent off.[60] Afterwards, Ronaldo publicly asked for a transfer, saying that United had not supported him during the incident.[61] United denied his request.[62] Although his World Cup altercation with Rooney resulted in Ronaldo being booed throughout the 2006–07 season,[63] he scored 20 league goals for the first time as United won the Premier League title.[64]

Ronaldo scored his first hat-trick for United in a 6–0 win against Newcastle United on 12 January 2008.[71] His 31 league goals in the season earned him the Premier League Golden Boot,[72] and he became the first winger to win the European Golden Shoe.[73] For the second consecutive season, he received the PFA Players' Player of the Year award and the FWA Footballer of the Year award.[74][75] On 21 May, United defeated Chelsea in the Champions League final in a penalty shoot-out after a 1–1 draw, with Ronaldo scoring his team's only goal.[H] As the Champions League top scorer, Ronaldo was named the UEFA Club Footballer of the Year.[79] Ronaldo became United's first Ballon d'Or winner since George Best in 1968,[80] and the first Premier League player to be named the FIFA World Player of the Year.[81]

Shortly after, United alleged that Real Madrid was pursuing Ronaldo, and filed a tampering complaint with FIFA. The governing body declined to take action against Madrid, and Ronaldo remained at United for another year.[82][83] In the 2009 Champions League, his match-winning goal against Porto earned him the inaugural FIFA Puskás Award, which recognises the best goal of the year.[84][85]

In 2009, Ronaldo transferred to Real Madrid for £80 million, a world record transfer fee at the time.[86] He was unveiled in front of 80,000 fans at the Santiago Bernabéu, and said that playing for Real Madrid had been his childhood dream.[87][88] He made his La Liga debut against Deportivo La Coruña on 29 August, scoring once in a 3–2 win.[89] He became the first Madrid player to scored in each of his first four league games.[90] He scored his first two Champions League goals for the club in September, in the first group match against Zürich.[91] In October, he suffered an ankle injury while on international duty, which kept him sidelined for seven weeks.[92][93] He finished the season with 33 goals across all competitions.[94]

Following Raúl's departure from the club, Ronaldo was given the No. 7 shirt for the 2010–11 season. He scored 53 goals during the season and earned his first trophy in Spain as Madrid won the Copa del Rey.[95] He became the first player to score 40 goals in a La Liga season.[96] In addition to the Pichichi Trophy, Ronaldo won the European Golden Shoe for a second time, becoming the first player to win the award in different leagues.[97]

During the 2011–12 season, Ronaldo scored 60 goals across all competitions and led Madrid to their first league title in four years with a record 100 points.[98] He finished runner-up for the 2011 FIFA Ballon d'Or behind Lionel Messi.[99] He scored his 100th league goal for Madrid in a 5–1 win over Real Sociedad on 24 March 2012, breaking the previous club record held by Ferenc Puskás.[100] In the 2012–13 season, Ronaldo scored his first hat-trick in the Champions League in a 4–1 win over Ajax.[101] Ronaldo finished second in voting for the 2012 FIFA Ballon d'Or, again behind Messi.[102] On 6 January, he captained Madrid for the first time in an official match, scoring twice in a 4–3 win over Sociedad.[103][104]

During the 2013–14 season, Madrid's attacking trio of Ronaldo, Gareth Bale and Karim Benzema was popularly dubbed "BBC" (an acronym of Bale, Benzema and Cristiano).[105] Ronaldo scored 69 goals in 2013, winning the 2013 FIFA Ballon d'Or.[106][107] In 2014, he helped Madrid win their tenth UEFA Champions League title, scoring once in their 4–1 final win over Atlético Madrid.[108] As the competition's top goalscorer for the third time, with a record 17 goals, he was named the UEFA Best Player in Europe.[109][110] He scored 31 goals in 30 league games during the season, which earned him the European Golden Shoe (shared with Luis Suárez) and the Pichichi Trophy.[111] On 4 May, he scored a back-heeled volley in the closing moments of a match against Valencia, which was voted the goal of the season by the Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional (LFP),[112] earning him the Best Player in La Liga award.[113]

During the 2014–15 season, Ronaldo set a new personal best of 61 goals. After winning the 2014 FIFA Club World Cup,[114] Ronaldo received the 2014 Ballon d'Or.[115][116] He finished as top scorer in the Champions League for a third consecutive season, with 10 goals (tied with Messi and Neymar).[117] On 5 April, he scored five goals in a game for the first time in his career, including an eight-minute hat-trick, in a 9–1 win over Granada.[118] His 300th goal for Madrid followed three days later in a 2–0 win against Rayo Vallecano.[119] He finished the season with 48 league goals, winning a second consecutive Pichichi Trophy and the European Golden Shoe for a record fourth time.[120]

Ronaldo became Real Madrid's all-time top scorer on 12 September 2015 against Espanyol, his 230 goals surpassing the total of the previous record holder, Raúl.[121] He also became the all-time top scorer in the Champions League with a hat-trick in the first group match against Shakhtar Donetsk in the 2015–16 competition.[122] Two goals against Malmö FF in a 2–0 win on 30 September saw him reach 500 career goals for club and country.[123] In the Champions League final, Ronaldo scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out against city rivals Atlético Madrid, winning his third Champions League title. He won the 2016 Ballon d'Or and the inaugural Best FIFA Men's Player.[124]

In the 2016–17 UEFA Champions League quarter-finals against Bayern Munich in April 2017, Ronaldo scored both goals in a 2–1 win which saw him become the first player to reach 100 goals in UEFA club competition.[125] On 17 May, he scored twice against Celta de Vigo to surpass Jimmy Greaves as the all-time top scorer in the top five European leagues.[126] He finished the season with 42 goals in all competitions and helped Madrid win the La Liga title.[127] In the 2017 Champions League final, Ronaldo scored two goals in a 4–1 victory over Juventus to bring him to 12 goals for the season, making him the competition's top goalscorer for the fifth straight season.[128]

On 23 October, his performances throughout 2017 saw him awarded The Best FIFA Men's Player award for the second consecutive year.[129] A day later, Ronaldo won the 2017 Ballon d'Or, receiving his fifth-time award on the Eiffel Tower in Paris.[130] On 3 April 2018, Ronaldo scored the first two goals in a 3–0 away win against Juventus in the quarter-finals of the 2017–18 UEFA Champions League, with his second goal being an acrobatic bicycle kick. Described as a "PlayStation goal" by Juventus defender Andrea Barzagli, with Ronaldo's foot approximately 7 ft 7 in (2.31 m) off the ground, it garnered him a standing ovation from the opposing fans in the stadium as well as a plethora of plaudits from peers, pundits and coaches.[131]

In the final on 26 May, Madrid defeated Liverpool 3–1, winning Ronaldo his fifth Champions League title, the first player to do so.[132] He finished as the top scorer of the tournament for the sixth consecutive season with 15 goals.[133] After the final, Ronaldo referred to his time with Madrid in the past tense, sparking speculation that he could leave the club.[134]

Ronaldo joined Juventus in 2018 for €100 million, the transfer was the highest ever for a player over 30 years old and the highest paid by an Italian club.[135] Upon signing, Ronaldo cited his need for a new challenge as his rationale for departing Madrid,[136] but later attributed the transfer to the lack of support he felt was shown by club president Florentino Pérez.[137] On 18 August, Ronaldo made his debut in a 3–2 away win against Chievo Verona.[138] On 19 September, in his first Champions League match for Juve, he was sent off against Valencia, his first red card in 154 Champions League appearances.[139] In the reverse (home) leg against Valencia, Cristiano won 100 Champions League matches, becoming the first ever player to do so.[140]

Ronaldo won his first trophy with the club on 16 January 2019, the 2018 Supercoppa Italiana, after he scored the only goal from a header against AC Milan.[141] On 10 February, Ronaldo scored in a 3–0 win over Sassuolo, the ninth consecutive away game in which he had scored in the league, equalling Giuseppe Signori's single season Serie A record of most consecutive away games with at least one goal.[142] On 12 March, Ronaldo scored a hat-trick in a 3–0 home win against Atlético in the second leg of the Champions League round of 16, helping Juventus overcome a two-goal deficit to reach the quarter-finals.[143] On 20 April, Ronaldo played in the scudetto clinching game against Fiorentina, as Juventus won their eighth successive title after a 2–1 home win, thereby becoming the first player to win league titles in England, Spain and Italy.[144] With 21 goals and eight assists, Ronaldo won the league award for Most Valuable Player.[145]

On 1 October, he reached several milestones in Juventus's 3–0 Champions League group stage win over Bayer Leverkusen including breaking Iker Casillas' record for most Champions League wins of all time.[146] On 18 December, Ronaldo leapt to a height of 8 ft 5 in (2.57 m), higher than the crossbar, to head the winning goal in a 2–1 away win against Sampdoria.[147] He scored his first Serie A hat-trick on 6 January 2020, in a 4–0 home win against Cagliari and became only the second player to score hat-tricks in the Premier League, La Liga and Serie A.[148] On 22 February, Ronaldo scored for a record-equalling 11th consecutive league game, alongside Gabriel Batistuta and Fabio Quagliarella, in what was his 1,000th senior professional game, a 2–1 away win against SPAL.[149]

Ronaldo scored six goals in the competition.[192] At the close of the year, Ronaldo had scored 54 goals in all competitions for Al-Nassr and Portugal, making him the outright top scorer in 2023, reaching the same goalscoring record as in 2016.[193][194] On 27 May 2024, in Al-Nassr's home fixture against Al-Ittihad, Ronaldo scored his 34th and 35th league goals of the campaign, surpassing Abderrazak Hamdallah's record for the most goals scored in a single Saudi Pro League season. He also became the first footballer to finish as top scorer in four different leagues: the English, Spanish, Italian and Saudi leagues.[195] On 31 May, in a 5–4 penalty shoot-out defeat to Al-Hilal in the 2024 King Cup final following a 1–1 draw after extra time (in which he scored his side's second spot kick), he equalled Rogério Ceni's record for most top-level matches by a male professional footballer (1,225).[196]

On 30 January 2025, he became the first player to reach 700 club-level wins, while also scoring a goal in a 2–1 away victory against Al Raed.[197] On 28 February, Ronaldo played his 100th match in all competitions for Al-Nassr, a 2–1 away loss to Al-Orobah.[198] On 26 May, he scored his 800th career club goal in a 3–2 away loss to Al Fateh on the final day of the season.[199] After the match, he hinted at his departure,[200] but ended up extending his contract with Al Nassr until 2027.[201] Despite that, he finished the 2024–25 season with 25 league goals, becoming the league's top scorer for a second consecutive time.[202]
